1196884496240586752.a: Prototyping hardware for a security camera using salvaged components and a $2 webcam. A super cheap (< $10) hardware platform to explore how to build a webcam OS that's hopefully not as easy to hack as many commercial devices. #makers #makerspace #armbian #debian #linux #infosec t.co

1196884511222575112.a: Video resolution aside, this camera is handy mostly because it is $2 and has no Infrared filter. It also includes Infrared LEDs which work surprisingly well. But I need to drive them with a 3.3V PWM signal. Probing with high current continuity test lets me find connection points. t.co

1196884522605912064.a: I found a random transistor on the floor and stuck it on a component tester to identify it. Conveniently, it says it's a BJT-NPN with 567mV base-emitter voltage. Wired that up according to this schematic I drew in my own copy of the infamous #DaveCAD. t.co

1196884528415072256.a: After imaging Armbian (Debian) Minimal onto an Orange Pi Zero & enabling some hardware overlays for GPIO and PWM I wrote a simple test script in Python to wiggle pin 7 in some interesting ways. 100Hz at 90% duty cycle, 20% duty then 10 Hz (warning: flashes may occur in next post) t.co
